title: The Rumor
text:
The first rumor said Sera was engaged.

The second said Rhen was the groom.

The third said they had already married.

Sera read the paper twice.

Rhen drank tea.

[[speaker:sera]]“Did you start this?”

She narrowed her eyes.

[[speaker:sera]]“Would you?”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Probably not.”

By sunset, the rumor had reached three provinces.

Sera folded the latest letter.

[[speaker:sera]]“Apparently our wedding is next month.”

Rhen looked up.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Should I prepare?”

She stared at him.

Then burst out laughing.

[[speaker:sera]]“You are getting dangerous.”

The rumor reached the tea shop before breakfast. Two customers bowed to Sera, congratulated Rhen, and left a ceremonial red envelope. Sera kept the envelope. Rhen kept looking at it.

The rumor's first practical consequence arrived before noon.

A noble messenger delivered a formal gift basket addressed to “Lady Sera and Master Rhen.”

Sera read the tag.

Rhen looked at the basket.

[[speaker:rhen]]“We received fruit.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Apparently marriage improves nutrition.”

He picked up a pear.

Sera slapped his hand.

[[speaker:sera]]“Evidence.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“You say that about everything you want to keep.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Correct.”

At the bottom of the basket she found a second letter, this one asking whether their supposed union changed the Pale Orchid's political allegiance.

The joke suddenly had teeth.

Sera folded the letter.

[[speaker:sera]]“There it is.”

[[speaker:sera]]“The reason someone started this.”

The rumor was no longer merely embarrassing.

Someone was testing how courts would react if the Pale Orchid and the hidden physician were treated as one political unit.

title: A Banquet
text:
Sera and Rhen attended a noble banquet together.

They were seated beside one another.

Someone called Rhen her husband.

Sera did not correct them.

Rhen nearly choked on tea.

She whispered:

[[speaker:sera]]“Behave.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“You caused this.”

At the banquet's end, an elderly duchess pressed a wedding gift into Sera's hands.

Sera accepted it.

Rhen waited until they were outside.

[[speaker:rhen]]“You didn't correct her.”

Sera tucked the gift under one arm.

[[speaker:sera]]“I liked the tea set.”

At the banquet, Sera discovered three noble families had rearranged their seating plans purely to place themselves closer to the supposed couple. She and Rhen spent the evening switching seats just to watch the confusion spread.

The banquet gave Sera an unexpected advantage.

People spoke more freely around couples.

Especially couples they assumed were too distracted by one another to listen.

So Sera leaned toward Rhen, smiled sweetly, and whispered:

[[speaker:sera]]“The man behind you is discussing troop movements.”

Rhen poured her tea.

[[speaker:rhen]]“The woman beside him has a concealed letter in her left sleeve.”

Sera's smile widened.

From across the hall, they looked affectionate.

Up close, they were conducting surveillance.

An elderly duchess stopped beside them.

[[speaker:duchess]]“You two suit each other.”

Sera opened her mouth.

Then closed it.

She took his arm instead.

[[speaker:sera]]“Thank you.”

The duchess left.

Rhen remained very still.

[[speaker:rhen]]“That was deliberate.”

Sera kept hold of his arm.

[[speaker:sera]]“Maybe.”

His smile followed them for the rest of the evening.

title: The Red Snow Widow
text:
Seo Haejin — the **Red Snow Widow**, the old-war assassin who spent years trying to kill Rhen before becoming a dangerous neutral ally — had first returned to Sera's life during the old Red Snow conflicts.

Seo Haejin arrived wearing red.

Seo Haejin — the Red Snow Widow — had first entered their lives during the old Red Snow troubles. The assassin had spent years trying to kill Rhen, saved his life anyway when it mattered, and somehow ended up as a sharp-tongued neutral ally who took far too much pleasure in Sera and Rhen's awkward courtship.

She knew Rhen from an older life.

She immediately noticed Sera.

[[speaker:haejin]]“So this is her.”

Sera smiled pleasantly.

[[speaker:sera]]“And you are?”

Haejin smiled.

[[speaker:haejin]]“Someone who knew him before you.”

Sera's smile became sweeter.

Rhen looked concerned.

Haejin watched Sera follow Rhen across the courtyard with her eyes.

[[speaker:haejin]]“You know he notices battle formations faster than that.”

Sera folded her arms.

[[speaker:haejin]]“Tragic.”

Sera glared.

Haejin smiled.

The Red Snow Widow had discovered her favorite new form of entertainment.

Haejin remembered exactly how awkward Rhen had been around affection decades earlier and considered his current state a dramatic improvement. Sera demanded examples. Rhen attempted to leave the room.

Haejin's arrival created immediate chaos because she treated the rumor as established fact.

[[speaker:haejin]]“Congratulations.”

Sera nearly dropped a cup.

[[speaker:sera]]“On what?”

[[speaker:haejin]]“Your wedding.”

[[speaker:sera]]“There is no wedding.”

Haejin looked at Rhen.

[[speaker:haejin]]“You proposed badly?”

[[speaker:rhen]]“I have not proposed.”

Haejin stared at him in disbelief.

[[speaker:haejin]]“After all this time?”

Sera turned bright red.

Rhen looked genuinely trapped.

For the next hour Haejin recounted old stories about Rhen avoiding romantic attention by disappearing into war zones.

Sera listened far too closely.

[[speaker:rhen]]“You are enjoying this.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Immensely.”

Haejin leaned across the table.

[[speaker:haejin]]“He once hid on a monastery roof for two days.”

Rhen closed his eyes.

Sera laughed until she cried.

title: Jealous Tea
text:
Sera was jealous.

She denied it.

Rhen did not notice.

Haejin noticed.

She laughed so hard she nearly dropped her cup.

[[speaker:haejin]]“Nothing.”

[[speaker:sera]]“You are smiling.”

[[speaker:haejin]]“Because you're adorable.”

Sera turned to Rhen.

[[speaker:sera]]“You.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Learn faster.”

That evening, Sera served Rhen tea without speaking.

He tasted it.

Too bitter.

[[speaker:rhen]]“You're still not jealous?”

[[speaker:sera]]“Correct.”

He took another sip.

[[speaker:rhen]]“The tea disagrees.”

Sera took the cup away.

[[speaker:sera]]“Then make your own.”

Sera's jealousy became impossible to hide when she sweetened Haejin's tea instead of Rhen's by mistake. Haejin noticed immediately and drank the entire cup with unbearable satisfaction.

Sera's jealousy became obvious only because Haejin knew exactly where to press.

She complimented Rhen's hair.

Sera stirred her tea harder.

She mentioned an old woman who had once tried to marry him.

Sera broke the sugar cube in half.

Haejin finally smiled.

[[speaker:haejin]]“You're very subtle.”

[[speaker:sera]]“About what?”

[[speaker:haejin]]“Nothing.”

Later, Rhen found Sera reorganizing shelves with unnecessary aggression.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Did I do something?”

[[speaker:rhen]]“That sounds dangerous.”

Sera turned.

[[speaker:sera]]“Did you really hide on a monastery roof?”

[[speaker:rhen]]“It was raining.”

Sera stared.

Then laughed despite herself.

Jealousy dissolved into amusement.

Mostly.

title: The Walk Home
text:
Rhen finally understood.

He caught up with Sera.

[[speaker:rhen]]“You were jealous.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“You were.”

She stopped.

Then grabbed his hand.

[[speaker:sera]]“Maybe.”

She continued walking.

Rhen followed.

Neither let go.

They walked home hand in hand.

Halfway there, Rhen stopped.

Sera looked back.

[[speaker:rhen]]“I like this.”

She looked at their hands.

Then at him.

She stepped closer.

[[speaker:sera]]“Because I'm not stopping.”

On the walk home, Sera swung their joined hands once like a much younger woman and immediately looked embarrassed. Rhen pretended not to notice. The smile on his face ruined the effort.

Their walk home stretched deliberately.

Sera chose the longer road.

He did not mention it.

When the street became crowded, Sera took his hand.

At first it was practical.

Then the crowd thinned.

She kept holding it.

Rhen looked down.

[[speaker:rhen]]“We have space now.”

They walked another block.

Sera swung their joined hands once.

Immediately regretted it.

Rhen's smile became unbearable.

[[speaker:sera]]“Say nothing.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“I wasn't going to.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Your face is talking.”

He squeezed her hand.

Sera squeezed back.

For the rest of the walk, neither pretended it was about the crowd.

title: The Golden Fox
text:
Qiao Ren introduced himself during a card game.

Qiao Ren, the Golden Fox, was a high-Marquis information broker rather than a battlefield conqueror. His strength was rumor architecture: he could turn gossip, half-truths and political incentives into pressure powerful enough to move sects and courts without drawing a weapon.

He had built half the rumors deliberately.

Sera challenged him.

He lost.

He laughed.

[[speaker:qiao]]“You are much scarier than the stories.”

Qiao Ren lost the card game and three political secrets.

Sera collected both.

[[speaker:qiao]]“You cheat.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Prove it.”

Qiao smiled.

Across the room, Rhen was already examining the rumor ledger Sera had won.

One line had been circled in gold.

ENGAGEMENT CONFIRMATION PENDING.

Sera saw it.

She did not cross it out.

Qiao Ren tried to sell Sera three versions of the same rumor. She bought the cheapest one, proved all three came from him, and charged him tea for the privilege of being exposed.

Qiao Ren did not look like a dangerous man.

That was deliberate.

He wore expensive but forgettable clothes, laughed easily, and never sat where someone could observe both his hands.

Sera noticed all of that before the first card was dealt.

[[speaker:sera]]“The Golden Fox.”

His eyes sharpened.

[[speaker:qiao]]“You know me.”

[[speaker:sera]]“You made sure I would.”

The game lasted forty minutes.

Qiao won the first three hands.

Sera won the next six.

By the final round she had taken his rumor ledger, two political contacts, and the name of the court official who first paid to spread the engagement story.

Rhen watched from nearby.

[[speaker:qiao]]“Does he always stare like that?”

[[speaker:sera]]“Only when I'm winning.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Frequently.”

Qiao finally understood why rumors about them were so easy to believe.

title: A Real Date
text:
Sera finally took Rhen somewhere with no investigation, enemy, political meeting or hidden agenda.

For their real date, she banned weapons at the table. Rhen obeyed literally and arrived without even a chopstick until she explained the rule had limits.

Their real date began badly.

Rhen arrived ten minutes early.

Sera arrived fifteen minutes early.

They found each other standing on opposite sides of the restaurant pretending neither had been nervous.

[[speaker:sera]]“You came early.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“So did you.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Coincidence.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Obviously.”

Sera had chosen a pale dress with no hidden blade sleeves.

Rhen noticed immediately.

[[speaker:rhen]]“You look beautiful.”

She blinked.

No teasing.

No evasive answer.

Just the truth.

Sera looked away.

[[speaker:sera]]“That was... acceptable.”

During dinner they talked about nothing important.

Tea.

Weather.

A ridiculous traveling play.

For once, Rhen did not tell a war story.

For once, Sera did not ask about an old mystery.

When they left, she slipped her hand into his as naturally as breathing.

title: Ask Properly
text:
They sat beneath lanterns.

Sera took his hand.

[[speaker:sera]]“If you ever ask me something important…”

[[speaker:sera]]“Ask properly.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“I will.”

Under the lanterns, Rhen watched Sera disappear into the tea shop.

She reopened the door.

[[speaker:sera]]“Tomorrow.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Tomorrow?”

[[speaker:sera]]“Practice.”

He looked confused.

[[speaker:sera]]“Asking properly.”

The door closed.

Rhen stood outside realizing, perhaps for the first time, that Sera was absolutely serious.

Sera practiced the words 'ask properly' alone upstairs and discovered they sounded much more frightening when she imagined Rhen actually doing it.

Sera's instruction to “ask properly” haunted Rhen for the entire evening.

He asked Luo Wen what properly meant.

Luo stared at him.

[[speaker:luo]]“You came to a physician for romantic advice?”

[[speaker:rhen]]“You speak to people.”

[[speaker:luo]]“So do bakers.”

Rhen considered asking a baker.

Luo stopped him.

Meanwhile, Sera was upstairs pretending not to listen through the floorboards.

Rhen eventually returned to the main room with several terrible ideas.

Kneeling.

Flowers.

A formal letter.

Possibly a sword.

Sera descended halfway down the stairs.

[[speaker:sera]]“No sword.”

Rhen looked up.

[[speaker:rhen]]“You were listening.”

[[speaker:sera]]“The floor is thin.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“It is not.”

[[speaker:sera]]“No sword.”

title: The Rumor Becomes Useful
text:
The marriage rumor accidentally prevented three political factions from approaching Sera.

Instead of correcting it, she used it.

Rhen found this amusing.

[[speaker:rhen]]“We're weaponizing our relationship.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Efficiently.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“I approve.”

The wedding rumor prevented a diplomatic ambush by making three factions assume Sera already had stronger political protection than they could offer.

She found that extremely funny.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Our imaginary marriage is useful.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Very.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Should we keep it?”

Sera looked at him.

[[speaker:sera]]“The rumor?”

[[speaker:sera]]“Careful.”

Three factions withdrew marriage proposals meant for Sera after deciding the rumor was credible. She celebrated by placing all three unopened letters under a wobbly table leg.

Once Sera understood the rumor's political utility, she became ruthless about it.

One faction attempted to pressure her into signing an alliance.

[[speaker:sera]]“My fiancé dislikes contracts.”

Rhen, standing beside her, almost choked.

The faction withdrew immediately.

Outside, he looked at her.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Fiancé?”

[[speaker:sera]]“Strategic terminology.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Of course.”

She linked her arm through his.

[[speaker:sera]]“Do you object?”

Rhen looked ahead.

Sera's smile softened.

For the first time, the rumor stopped feeling like something happening to them.

Sera had chosen to use it.

And somewhere along the way, the word itself had stopped sounding entirely fictional.

title: The Quiet Proposal
text:
At the tea shop after closing, Rhen finally asked:

[[speaker:rhen]]“Would you want to marry me?”

Sera froze.

[[speaker:sera]]“Ask me properly.”

Rhen stood.

He took her hand.

For once, he looked nervous.

Sera laughed softly.

She did not answer yet.

She kissed his forehead.

[[speaker:sera]]“Try again tomorrow.”

Rhen rehearsed the question once after Sera went upstairs.

Haejin, unfortunately, was still in the shop.

[[speaker:haejin]]“Too formal.”

Rhen stared at her.

[[speaker:rhen]]“How long have you been there?”

[[speaker:haejin]]“Long enough.”

Upstairs, Sera heard every word.

She buried her face in a pillow so nobody would hear her laughing.

Rhen spent half the night deciding whether a proper question required kneeling. Haejin offered conflicting advice on purpose. Upstairs, Sera heard enough to realize tomorrow would be entertaining.

Rhen's attempt at a proper proposal did not happen that night.

Not because he lost his nerve.

Because Sera stopped him.

He had prepared flowers.

A clean table.

Even a speech.

Sera entered, saw everything, and immediately understood.

Rhen stood.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Sera—”

She crossed the room and put one finger against his lips.

[[speaker:sera]]“Tomorrow.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Because tonight I want this.”

She sat beside him.

Took his hand.

Rested her head against his shoulder.

No audience.

No rumor.

No political meaning.

Just them.

[[speaker:sera]]“Ask me when it doesn't feel like the whole world is waiting for the answer.”

Rhen relaxed.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Tomorrow, then.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Maybe.”

He laughed.

She smiled against his shoulder.
